item.title: Toyin Agbetu - The Dark Knight Rises
item.description: Label: D3 Elements | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: D3 Elements

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

D3 (a French label, pronounced natively as deeh-trois, which is how you say Detroit in the same language. Cool, huh?) is back with a new drop on its Classic Edition series. After 'Kreme de la Kreme' comes Toyin Agbetu's 'The Dark Knight Rises' 12?, a collection of four deep tracks newly remastered from original DAT tapes. Cuts like 'I Do Believe' and 'Party Time' sit comfortably in the realm of classic soulful house - humid, heady, warm - while 'U Gotta Slow Down', released under Agbetu's Nemesis alias, makes its vinyl debut, adding rarity value for collectors and raved up old school house for dancers. K15's reinterpretation of 'Piece of Mind' brings a spacious, broken-beat perspective. The original version is equally rhythmically fresh.

  • A1.Piece Of Mind
  • A2. Piece Of Mind (K15 Reiniterpretation)
  • B1. U Gotta Slow Down
  • B2. Party Time
  • B3. I Do Believe

item.title: Cassio - Baby Love
item.description: Label: Groovin Records | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: House , Deep House , Garage House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Groovin Records

Prix: 14,00 €

Style: House , Deep House , Garage House

Repress alert! NYC underground legend Cassio Ware's seminal house classic from 1992 is back on the shelves for a limited time only. His unmistakable vocals are supported by Blaze's timeless production across all five brilliant versions. "Baby Love (Asia Iman)" is full of uplifting house pianos, brass section and swing fuelled rhythms, as does "Elan Imari" but for many its all about the dub version which gets properly deep and Baby Donovan's Mix which gets more tough and street sounding.

item.title: Julie Brannen - I'll Be Good To You ( Kerri Chandler Rmx)
item.description: Label: Groovin Records | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: Classic House, Garage , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Groovin Records

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: Classic House, Garage , Deep House

While Italo-house of the early to mid 1990s was a distinctive sound, it owed a great deal to NYC and NJ garage-house, with many of the finest records being closer in sound and feel to their American counterparts than the country's earlier "dream house" wave (think Sueno Latino and Don Carlos). Julie Brannen's 1993 gem, reissued here for the first time by Groovin', is a fantastic example of this. It brings together the three most loved of the numerous remixes that appeared at the time. The Italian production team behind it's own 'Deep is Good Mix' - an organ-rich slab of tactile and rolling garage-house deepness - is accompanied by two vintage Kerri Chandler tweaks: the warm, breezy, colourful and jazzy 'Feel mix', no doubt an anthem at NYC's Shelter club, and the bouncier, organ-rich '6:23 Again mix'.

Tracklist:

  • A1. I'll Be Good To You (Feel mix)
  • B1. I'll Be Good To You (6:23 Again mix)
  • B2. I'll Be Good To You (Deep Is Good mix)

item.title: Peven Everett - Stuck
item.description: Label: Groovin Records | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Groovin Records

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

20 years after it first landed on Bobby and Steve's Soul Heaven Records imprint - once the UK's foremost soulful house outlet - Peven Everett's 'Stuck' returns to stores via a must-check reissue specialists Groovin' Records. Wisely, the Italian outfit has chosen to showcase two of the more celebrated and sought-after rubs. On side A, Danny Krivit delivers a lovely 12-minute edit in which Everett's effortlessly soulful vocals ride hypnotic, soft-touch drums, jazzy guitar licks, warming bass guitar and jammed-out electric piano keys. Krivit's version has long been an anthem at Body & Soul NYC and remains a fine, stretched-out revision. The late Phil Asher takes over on side B, balancing soulful deep house jazziness with a more driving garage-house groove.

Tracklist:

  • A1. Stuck (Danny Krivit re-edit)
  • B1. Stuck (Phil Asher's Soul Heaven remix)

item.title: Various - Indulgence Records - The Sampler
item.description: Label: Indulgence | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: House , Chicago Style
item.content:encoded:
Label: Indulgence

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: House , Chicago Style

Indulgence know what they're doing. Following the well-received DJ Split 12", this six-track sampler doubles down on the label's commitment to early house done with deep understanding rather than lazy imitation. DJ Split's 'Tape Zone Xoxo Mix' sets the tone and is a popping, raw and proudly analogue jacker. The standout is Raymond Owen's 'Beyond The Pleasure', laced with subtle breaks, infectious bleeps and the unmistakable DNA of Northern UK club culture. Elsewhere, Ba.dido and David Boning bring depth, Toby Simpson's 'Temptations' does exactly what the name suggests and Jimm's Feela closes things out with soul to spare. Real deal house.

item.title: Roy Ayers Ubiquity - Change Up The Groove (Remastered)
item.description: Label: Vampi Soul | Prix: 40,00 € | Style: Funk
item.content:encoded:
Label: Vampi Soul

Prix: 40,00 €

Style: Funk

First released in 1974 during his early Polygram run, Change Up The Groove finds Roy Ayers Ubiquity deep in the pocket between jazz finesse and funk muscle. Ayers' vibraphone work threads through arrangements driven by Bernard Purdie's precision drumming, with strings adding a stealthier warmth about the edges. The set moves from the slick, percussive strut of the title track to the supple swing of 'Sensitize', a cover of Stevie Wonder's 'Don't You Worry 'Bout A Thing', and the cinematic 'Mash Theme'. His version of 'Feel Like Makin' Love' hums with soft electric glow, while 'The Boogie Back' rides a breakbeat that's fed countless hip-hop samples. This 2025 Vampisoul reissue comes on LP, restoring a key chapter in Ayers' shift toward 70s funk.

item.title: The Other People Place - Lifestyles Of The Laptop Café
item.description: Label: Warp | Prix: 45,00 € | Style: Electro
item.content:encoded:
Label: Warp

Prix: 45,00 €

Style: Electro

Last year, someone set up an online petition calling for Warp to re-release The Other People Place's brilliant Lifestyles Of The Laptop Cafe album on wax. Happily, Warp has responded to the strength of feeling from electronica fans - most of whom bristled at the high online prices for second hand copies - and re-pressed it. Drexciya man James Stinson's 2001 solo set remains a timeless electronic classic; a perfectly pitched and immaculately produced fusion of downtempo electro rhythms, spacey electronics and twinkling synthesizer melodies. In fact, you'll struggle to find a better electro album full stop, making this reissue an essential purchase for anyone not lucky enough to own an original copy.

item.title: Various Artists - Strange Weather: A Different Kettle Of Fish (feat Housey Doingz, The Ron Honey Experience, Space Bunny)
item.description: Label: Sushitech | Prix: 50,00 € | Style: Tech House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Sushitech

Prix: 50,00 €

Style: Tech House

Laurant Webb, Dave Coker, Justin Bailey, and Dave Pine were the key figures behind Strange Weather Studios, which was a creative hub in Southeast London that helped shape the very early sound of tech house in the capital. Collaborating with friends and partners on several projects, they produced a number of influential records that defined the genre including under aliases such as Housey Doingz, 7th Voyage, and Space Bunny. This release on Sushitech, which always does a fine job of offering up the best tech house past and present, pays tribute to the studio and its collaborators with representative tracks carefully selected by Laurant Webb and label head Yossi Amoyal. Restored and remastered from rare DATs and pressed up to no fewer than six sides of vinyl, it's a great look at a significant moment in the evolution of tech house.

item.title: Norman Connors - Mr C (reissue)
item.description: Label: Bewith | Prix: 40,00 € | Style: Funk , Disco Funk
item.content:encoded:
Label: Bewith

Prix: 40,00 €

Style: Funk , Disco Funk

Norman Connors, the Philadelphia-born drummer and producer, may be best known for his jazz credentials, but this 1981 gem is a full-bodied plunge into post-disco boogie and slick street-funk. It opens with the radiant thump of 'She's Gone'-a Beau Williams-fronted burner driven by lush strings, sparkling Rhodes and a fat bassline built for roller rinks and basement parties alike. 'Party Town' brings synth-led bounce and slap-happy horns, while 'Keep Doin' It' floats in with satin groove and a vocal glide as effortless as its hook. Connors' use of drum machines and bright, tropical percussion on tracks like 'Stay With Me' shows a producer fully dialled into the era's shifting dancefloor codes. Side B leans in with the sultry 'Sing A Love Song' and the elevational 'Love's In Your Corner', featuring a show-stopping vocal from Jean Carn. The title cut is pure glide: a jazz-funk instrumental wrapped in understated class. This remastered reissue finds Connors' boogie-funk detour sounding sharper than ever-mature, playful, and deeply groovy.

item.title: Terry Francis - El Tel Collection
item.description: Label: Pariter | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: Tech House , Dub House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Pariter

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: Tech House , Dub House

The agenda-setting Sushitech has a just as influential sub-label, Pariter, which welcomes the one and only tech house instigator, Terry Francis, for a rare and essential reissue. Francis was there at the birth of original tech house with his killer Wiggle parties and fabric residency and now kicks off what will be a limited series that digs into his archives. These first offerings were originally released on Eukahouse 25 years ago, with opener 'Notice Board' bringing a thumping low end and wiggling bassline that is topped with smooth chord work. 'Hello, Acid Dathera' (unreleased retake version) is a busier sound with a tribal edge and restless drums and bass with acid daubs and crisp hi-hats, making it a full body workout.

item.description: Label: Be With | Prix: 35,00 € | Style: Jazz Funk , Disco Funk
item.content:encoded:

Philly supergroup MFSB (an acronym for Mother, Father, Sister, Brother,) ended their spectacular discography with this, Mysteries of the World, a magnificent final studio album, co-written and produced with the legendary Dexter Wansel. The title track is of course the well-known, much loved and sparkling jewel in the album's crown but the whole thing is a wonderful affair with Philly soul and orchestral jazz-funk meeting in perfect harmony. The stylish and sophisticated sounds here still sound out of this world and cannot fail to get any dancefloor going.

item.title: Byron The Aquarius - Global Caress
item.description: Label: Star Creature | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Star Creature

Prix: 22,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

We're big fans of US talent Byron The Aquarius here at Juno. He is a magician on the keys and so whatever grooves he lays down, they sparkle with melodic brightness. His latest on Star Creature is a brilliantly mixed back that starts with a pretty gritty and dark cut, 'Atliens To Detroit', full of menace and warehouse filth. Elsewhere, there are signature synth glows on the deep and brilliantly undercooked 'Everlasting' while 'Long Way Home' sucks into that sort of dreamy, widescreen and cosmic deep-jazz-house sounds that Larry Heard perfected aeons ago. 'Jamama' is a nice louche and playful closer with fizzy synth fun.

  • A2. Bob Power At It Again (NYC mix)
  • A3. Everlasting
  • B1. Fantasyies
